finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation, and returns the response body to the caller. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), and localhost, and read the responses.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the body echoed via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: Route /fetch registered with no auth middleware
target taken from the query string unmodified
http.Get(target) issued with no scheme, host or IP check; the default client follows redirects
Response body is returned to the attacker (full-read SSRF); the error text is also reflected at main.go:18

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, private-IP block, or auth on this path. The `allowed` map at main.go:9 is used only by safeFetch. No validation exists in `fetch`.

verdict.reason: main.go:15 reads the attacker-controlled `target` and main.go:16 passes it to http.Get with no validation, then main.go:22 returns the body; /fetch is registered at main.go:41 with no auth, and the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27).
